claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi has an fcc structure and qualifies as a high-entropy alloy.
Controlled nitriding during annealing can introduce nitrogen into interstitial sites in FeCoNi.
Interstitial nitrogen induces localized lattice strain and structural disorder in fcc FeCoNi.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy promotes domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases coercivity relative to untreated FeCoNi.
Nitrogen-doped FeCoNi will exhibit at least a 25% coercivity increase relative to the selected FeCoNi-based baseline.
Nitrogen-doped FeCoNi will retain high saturation magnetization.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
The proposed nitriding conditions can preserve the fcc structure.
The degree of coercivity enhancement depends on nitrogen partial pressure, annealing time, annealing temperature, and nitrogen-distribution uniformity.
The alloy can remain equiatomic and retain configurational entropy of at least 1.0R after nitrogen incorporation.

contradictions.description: The intervention adds nitrogen to the alloy, while the conditions and boundary state that nitriding must not alter the equiatomic composition. Adding an unspecified amount of nitrogen changes the full atomic composition unless 'equiatomic' is explicitly restricted to the Fe:Co:Ni sublattice.
